key_insight: Adaptive variational quantum chemistry can become trapped by the fermion-to-qubit mapping itself, with symmetry-preserving representations avoiding optimization flatness better than asymmetric encodings.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum algorithms, ansatz design must consider both molecular symmetry and qubit mapping, or training can fail even when the operator pool is symmetry-constrained.
method: Tested a spin-conserved SUSD operator pool on stretched LiH, BeH2, and H2O geometries.
Compared asymmetric distortions against a symmetric stretching baseline to isolate point-group symmetry effects.
Added a covariance-driven adaptive shot-allocation filter to prune low-signal channels and stop flatlined runs early.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic evaluation at 2× equilibrium bond stretching, showing optimization trapping in asymmetric cases under Bravyi-Kitaev mapping and better landscape protection for symmetric BeH2.
watch_item: The covariance-based pruning and termination logic may be sensitive to threshold tuning and could prematurely discard useful gradients in noisy hardware runs.
paper_title: Representation-Induced Symmetry Trapping in Adaptive Variational Quantum Simulations of Multi-Reference Topologies
